legend: Derivation of the waveform cohort and recorded infusion-adjustment subset. Exclusions in the left panel are sequential and mutually exclusive. The right panel distinguishes cases with target-pump records, observed rate changes, quality-eligible adjustment blocks, low-reference events and confirmed recoveries. Pump-record availability and event denominators are not interchangeable. MAP, mean arterial pressure.

Event visibility and aggregate exposure across sampling intervals. Panel a shows phase-averaged reference episodes represented by any low display, including inherited low values. Panel b shows displayed duration and deficit area as percentages of their respective continuous-reference totals. These quantities are on separate panels and do not share a clinical scale. Reference episodes lasted at least 60 s below 65 mmHg; duration and area include all low-pressure bins, including shorter runs. Unavailable initial display contributes no displayed burden. Uncertainty and unrounded values are in Supplemental Digital Content 1, Table S26. AUC, area under the deficit curve.

New low samples, inherited display and case-level heterogeneity with a 5 min display. Panel a assigns every phase-episode pair to one exclusive source category; a new low sample takes priority when both sources occur. Panel b shows the distribution of phase-averaged case miss proportions. Panel c shows the within-case maximum-minus-minimum phase range in percentage points. In panels b and c, the thick segment is the interquartile range and the point is the median; thin whiskers in panel b are the 5th and 95th percentiles, not confidence limits. All qualifying episodes lasted at least 60 s below 65 mmHg; case distributions include 1899 cases. Cases with few events can have wide phase ranges.

Display state at low-reference infusion adjustments and after recovery. Low reference denotes mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg. Panel a shows four exclusive phase-averaged states at 236 low-reference adjustments from 83 subjects; the 0.2% unavailable fraction at 5 min is included although too small to label inside the bar. A new low value was acquired during the current contiguous low run before adjustment; an inherited value came from before that run. Panel b shows mean restricted low-display persistence in 184 recovery events from 78 subjects; bars are 95% subject-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Recovery requires two consecutive normal completed bins. Observation ends at normal display, missing reference, recurrent hypotension or 5 min after adjustment. This is a recorded management context, not a treatment-effect estimate.
